input.explanation:
The fault is in deploy/values-production.yaml. Revision 0d8e826 changed `cache.port` from 6379 to 6380. The investigation's evidence shows every lookup being refused at redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380, while the cache itself is healthy. That points to 6379 as the port the cache listens on.

The change sets `cache.port` back to 6379 in deploy/values-production.yaml. Nothing else in that file changes.

I added tests/io_shop/test_deploy_values.py. It reads deploy/values-production.yaml, pulls out the keys under the top-level `cache:` block, and checks that `port` is 6379 and `host` is cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local. A wrong port doesn't make pages fail, only slow, so this test is what would catch the same edit in review before it ships. Against the file as it stands (6380) the port check should fail; with this change it should pass. Nothing has run it yet.

One caveat: if the cache is ever moved to 6380 on purpose, the test's `CACHE_PORT` constant has to be updated along with the cache itself.

files.content:
# Deployment configuration for the io-shop account service, production.
#
# Rendered into the cluster as a ConfigMap and mounted into the pod, which is
# why the service reads this file rather than being handed environment
# variables: the values here are the deployment's, not the code's, and changing
# one is a change to configuration that ships without the service being rebuilt.
#
# Owned by whoever runs the shop. Changes here go out the way any other change
# goes out - reviewed, merged, and synced by the platform - and land without a
# single line of io-shop's source being touched.

replicas: 3

resources:
  memoryLimitMiB: 2048

# How the platform scales the shop.
#
# Rendered into a HorizontalPodAutoscaler, so `replicas` above is only where the
# deployment starts: the controller decides the count from there, between the
# floor and the ceiling here, aiming to keep each replica at the CPU target.
#
# `scaleDownStabilizationSeconds` is how far back the controller looks before it
# believes a fall in load is real. Kubernetes defaults it to 300 - five minutes
# of the highest recommendation it saw - because a controller acting on the
# reading in front of it acts on a reading its own last action produced.
autoscaling:
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 6
  targetCpuPercent: 70
  scaleDownStabilizationSeconds: 0

# How the platform finds the shop's metrics.
#
# The shop exposes its per-minute figures on this port, and the scrape config
# selects the target by the port's *name* rather than its number - which is
# what lets the number move without anything having to be re-pointed at it.
#
# The name is therefore load-bearing in a way the number is not. Nothing in the
# shop reads it.
metrics:
  port: 9090
  portName: http-metrics

# Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
#
# The account page reads this cache before it works a shopper's spend figure
# out, and recomputes when the cache has nothing or cannot be reached. So the
# shop stays correct whatever is written here - it only stays *fast* while the
# address is right.
cache:
  host: cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local
  port: 6379

# Which model files a purchase under a category.
#
# Every version ships in the image beside the code, and this picks the one the
# shop loads - so moving to a new model is a change here, reviewed and synced
# like any other, and moving back is a rollback rather than a rebuild.
categoriser:
  model: v2

input.summary: Point the summary cache back at port 6379 in production values
